title: Award-winning upgrade strengthens Hawaiian island’s water future
summary: Recognized as Project of the Year by the Hawaii Society of Professional Engineers, Jacobs led the transformation of Lahaina’s wastewater facility into a sustainable water source for West Maui, supporting recovery, conservation and long-term water security.
body_markdown:
An award-winning $14 million wastewater upgrade is securing West Maui’s water future. The Lahaina Wastewater Reclamation Facility (WWRF) R-1 Improvements Project was honored as the Hawaii Society of Professional Engineers Project of the Year 2026, recognizing its innovation, sustainability and community impact. By transforming aging 1970s infrastructure into a reliable


[recycled water](https://www.jacobs.com/solutions/water-reuse) source, the project is strengthening water security and reducing environmental impact, supporting a region navigating drought, climate pressures and


[wildfire recovery](https://www.jacobs.com/newsroom/news/restoring-lahaina-rapid-sewer-repairs-accelerate-community-recovery) .


### **Reliable water for a changing climate**


The upgraded facility now delivers a consistent supply of high-quality recycled water for golf courses, resorts, public parks and future agricultural use, reducing demand on Maui’s limited potable water resources.


By stabilizing treatment processes and eliminating damaging flow swings, the system produces dependable effluent that supports both daily operations and long-term recovery efforts across West Maui.


“This project is a meaningful step forward. By improving the reliability of our recycled water system, we’re better equipped to serve our community, protect our natural resources and


plan for the future


,” says County of Maui Wastewater Capital Improvement Program Manager Juan Rivera.


### **Less waste. More impact.**


The project significantly reduces reliance on injection wells, while protecting groundwater and coastal ecosystems, advancing Maui’s sustainability goals.


By repurposing existing basins,


channels


and infrastructure, we were able to minimize construction waste and reduce the project’s carbon footprint, while also lowering capital costs. This approach turned underutilized assets into a high-performing system that will continue delivering long-term operational savings.


“We did


more than upgrade a facility


—


we unlocked the value of infrastructure that was already there, making it more efficient, sustainable and resilient,” emphasizes Jacobs Vice President, Derek Ono.


### **Engineering stability behind the scenes**


Highly variable flows once disrupted treatment and damaged equipment. Today, advanced process modeling and integrated controls keep the system running smoothly, while a multi-layered automation system synchronizes pumps, valves and sensors, creating a smarter, more adaptable facility.


By transforming existing infrastructure into a resilient water solution, this award-winning project supports West Maui’s ability to adapt,


recover


and thrive.
